title: Seahorse Anatomy — A Guide’s Field Key

rows.text: The long snout ends in a small mouth used for suction feeding.
Bony plates form rings around the body beneath the skin.

rows.text: Specialized pigment cells help the skin change color for camouflage.

rows.text: The paired pectoral fins help with steering and control.

rows.text: The dorsal fin helps propel the seahorse through the water.

rows.text: Male seahorses brood developing young in a pouch.
rows.photo_note: This general fact does not identify the photographed animal’s sex or reproductive state.
